answer: One workable design: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because opal only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice quartz is enforced by the ledger itself: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
